loop.top3_why: The diagnosis recommends a weighted combination for this trend‑dominated, highly predictable series. Candidate B implements an inverse‑error weighted scheme on the same pool as the trimmed‑mean, providing a principled way to emphasize the better‑performing models while still allowing the weaker ones to contribute. Its per‑window performance is consistently close to the leader and the weighting scheme is expected to generalize better than a simple trimmed‑mean, which may discard useful information from the lower‑ranked models.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate A (trimmed‑mean) and C (mean) are deterministic baselines that ignore model performance differences. While they achieve very similar validation scores, the weighted approach aligns with the diagnostic hint and offers a more robust way to handle the moderate ranking stability and correlated errors observed in the model pool. Thus, B is preferred over A and C.
